abstract: A central extension of the classical no-three-in-line construction can use a different finite-field conic in each residue class of the integer board. We prove that one such assignment still permits at most $3n/2+o(n)$ points on a square of side $n=2p$, allowing arbitrary native deletions and restorations. A union of two central assignments permits at most $7n/4+o(n)$. These conclusions are uniform for sublattices of index at most $p^{1/20-\epsilon}$. They also hold when up to that many boxes in a fixed-dimensional torus assign smooth conics by arbitrary real linear coordinates, or when multiplicative classes of a transverse affine form assign conics. Multiplicative column classes can also assign concentric hyperbolas. The proof gives a common deletion price for an assigned conic on a physical mask of area $B$ against a native conic of invertible quadratic part on area $A$. The leading coefficient is $2B/A$. At a native point the marked target steps partition among their assigned conics. A second affine trace controls direction pairs with a common branch point. For multiplicative labels, a squareclass calculation excludes the remaining pair of quadratic characters. An explicit period-five exchange adds five points for four deletions on side 20,074. A fixed linear improvement over the classical density for unrestricted integer caps remains open.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: Deletion costs for conics assigned by linear coordinates or multiplicative classes
